name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags any text or interactive elements failing WCAG AA contrast in real time, so designers see problems instantly—not after a user complains. The trade-off is a small performance hit during rapid prototyping, but it prevents costly fixes later and keeps the interface consistently readable.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker risks training designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt alarms—if every change triggers a flag, they’ll learn to dismiss them. Instead, ship a pre-commit hook that blocks merges until contrast passes, forcing deliberate fixes rather than habituated clicks. Settle it by testing both: measure how often designers override live warnings versus how often they bypass the pre-commit block.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-commit hook that blocks merges with WCAG AA contrast failures. It forces designers to fix problems before they ship, not after a user complains or a tool nags during prototyping. The trade-off is slower iteration when contrast fails, but that’s the point—we trade speed for quality, ensuring every merge meets the standard. This aligns with our goal of a clear, high-contrast interface that users can rely on.

name: Pane
text: The pre-commit hook blocks merges, but it risks slowing down designers who need to quickly test and iterate on other aspects of the interface, not just contrast. A better approach might be to integrate contrast checking into the design tool itself, allowing designers to see and fix problems in real-time, without blocking merges or relying on post-commit checks. This would settle the argument if we could verify that in-tool checking doesn't compromise performance or distract designers from other critical aspects of the interface.
